market_question: US x Iran permanent peace deal by June 30, 2026?
reasoning: A permanent US-Iran peace deal ending all military hostilities would be historically unprecedented and requires resolving deep-seated issues (nuclear program, sanctions, regional proxies). The temporary ceasefire announced in April 2026 signals ongoing diplomacy, but the leap to a comprehensive permanent deal by June 30 is implausible given political opposition in both nations and the short timeframe.
evidence_points: The US and Iran have never signed a permanent peace agreement since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.
The mentioned April 7, 2026 ceasefire is explicitly temporary and would not qualify as a permanent peace deal under the resolution rules.
Hardline factions in Iran and US domestic political constraints (including Israeli influence) make a lasting accord extremely difficult to negotiate in a few months.
sources_consulted: General geopolitical analysis of Middle East peace prospects
